meetings.headline: Committee heard SEL (Trails to Wellness) presentation and a five-year staffing plan warning of grant-funded job losses in FY2025.
meetings.summary: The meeting centered on a staff presentation of the Trails to Wellness social emotional learning curriculum, with committee questions on data, opt-outs and high school teacher readiness. Administration then presented identified staffing needs over five years, stressing the loss of ESSER funding in the second year, new discipline-law staffing, and the need to lobby legislators. The committee approved minutes, a primary school line-item transfer, release of field-use data to the Parks Commission, and two donations, then adjourned.

what_happened.line: Administration presented a five-year staffing plan that warns of losing grant-funded positions when federal ESSER money ends, with the local budget unable to absorb them.
A member estimated the grant-funded positions at well over a million dollars; administration said the local budget cannot absorb them.
The committee voted unanimously by roll call on a primary school line-item transfer, release of field-use and permitting fee data to the Parks Commission, and two Turkey Hill donations.
The committee agreed to put a meeting with state legislators and the town manager, and Chapter 70 lobbying, on a future agenda.
Administration aims to present the proposed budget on January 4, with a hearing March 15 and the Finance Committee March 16.

why_it_matters: When federal ESSER money ends, positions it pays for must be cut or move onto the local budget, which is paid mostly by property taxes and could become a request residents are asked to vote on.
State aid, including Chapter 70, is set outside Lunenburg, so the committee's plan to lobby legislators bears on how much of the school budget falls on the tax bill.
watch_next: January 4 School Committee meeting, when administration aims to present the proposed budget.
March 15 budget hearing and the March 16 Finance Committee meeting.

what_happened.line: The committee approved a budget line-item transfer after the business manager explained the changes, including higher dues and a fire alarm item moved between accounts.
The five-year staffing plan and fiscal forecast were discussed at length with no resolution; the chair said they will be revisited at the next meeting.
The committee voted to authorize the chair to sign a letter on town building use and Turkey Hill, pending a rewrite and individual comments.
The committee accepted the FY23 quarterly budget report, which showed a negative long-term substitute balance and under-budgeted unemployment compensation.
The committee released the class of 2022 remaining funds and accepted a donation to the high school athletic department.

why_it_matters: The staffing plan is where the end of ESSER money meets the town's levy limit. A member said that without a replacement or an override the district would have fewer people in three years, and the plan stays undecided.
The building-use letter and Turkey Hill capital planning could lead to excludable debt or multi-year capital commitments, which would show up on tax bills, but the letter is still being rewritten.
watch_next: The next meeting is to revisit the five-year plan and forecast, with a goals check-in and a possible SEL curriculum presentation.
The chair's rewritten building-use letter, to be circulated for individual comments before it is signed and delivered.
